k: Your mother's herb garden. Rosemary gone to ash. Thyme gone to ash.
src: 'Your mother\'s herb garden. Rosemary gone to ash. Thyme gone to ash.'

k: And the sea-lavender — the one that never flowered in all the years you knew it — is covered in small purple flowers.
src: 'And the sea-lavender — the one that never flowered in all the years you knew it — is covered in small purple flowers.'

k: ...Now? Now you flower?
src: '...Now? Now you flower?'

k: Perhaps it was waiting for someone to come home and see.
src: 'Perhaps it was waiting for someone to come home and see.'

k: The lamp room of Lanternfall. The light is everywhere — in the walls, in the floor, in the air like warm water.
src: 'The lamp room of Lanternfall. The light is everywhere — in the walls, in the floor, in the air like warm water.'

k: At the heart of it, with her back to you and her hands lifted to the lamp, a woman in a Keeper's robe. Her braid has come undone. The light pours out of her hands and does not stop.
src: 'At the heart of it, with her back to you and her hands lifted to the lamp, a woman in a Keeper\'s robe. Her braid has come undone. The light pours out of her hands and does not stop.'

k: Wren?
src: 'Wren?'

k: Wren. You're late for supper.
src: 'Wren. You\'re late for supper.'

k: Come inside, little bird. It's getting dark. It's been getting dark for such a long time.
src: 'Come inside, little bird. It\'s getting dark. It\'s been getting dark for such a long time.'

k: Mom, you can let go now. The boat got away. We made it. I made it. It's been a whole year.
src: 'Mom, you can let go now. The boat got away. We made it. I made it. It\'s been a whole year.'

k: If I let go, the dark comes in.
src: 'If I let go, the dark comes in.'

k: If I let go, you'll leave. You always wanted to leave. You used to toddle to the end of the dock and just _look_.
src: 'If I let go, you\'ll leave. You always wanted to leave. You used to toddle to the end of the dock and just _look_.'

k: In Wren's pack, the little brass lantern her mother gave her flares, as if it has recognized someone.
src: 'In Wren\'s pack, the little brass lantern her mother gave her flares, as if it has recognized someone.'

k: Stay. I'll keep the light on. Nothing will take you. Not the sea. Not the Hierophant. Not _time_. You'll be sixteen forever, and I will never have to watch you go.
src: 'Stay. I\'ll keep the light on. Nothing will take you. Not the sea. Not the Hierophant. Not _time_. You\'ll be sixteen forever, and I will never have to watch you go.'

k: Wren. That is what he wants. That is Evernoon.
src: 'Wren. That is what he wants. That is Evernoon.'

k: ...She's not wrong, though. That's the worst part. Some days it's what I'd want too.
src: '...She\'s not wrong, though. That\'s the worst part. Some days it\'s what I\'d want too.'

k: But it isn't her. My mom never once asked me to stay. Not even at the dock. She wanted to, I _saw_ her want to. She gave me Dad's compass and she let me go.
src: 'But it isn\'t her. My mom never once asked me to stay. Not even at the dock. She wanted to, I _saw_ her want to. She gave me Dad\'s compass and she let me go.'

k: That's who you are, Mom. Not this. I'm going to get you back to who you are.
src: 'That\'s who you are, Mom. Not this. I\'m going to get you back to who you are.'

k: Then I will make you stay.
src: 'Then I will make you stay.'

k: The light gutters. The shadow that was wound around her peels away like wet paper, and burns, and is gone.
src: 'The light gutters. The shadow that was wound around her peels away like wet paper, and burns, and is gone.'

k: What is left is a tired woman kneeling on a stone floor, holding a lamp that is still, somehow, alight.
src: 'What is left is a tired woman kneeling on a stone floor, holding a lamp that is still, somehow, alight.'

k: ...Wren?
src: '...Wren?'

k: Oh. Look at you. You've grown. You— your _hair_. You cut it yourself, didn't you. It's terrible.
src: 'Oh. Look at you. You\'ve grown. You— your _hair_. You cut it yourself, didn\'t you. It\'s terrible.'

k: _(laughing, and not laughing)_ Ilse did the back.
src: '_(laughing, and not laughing)_ Ilse did the back.'

k: I did my best, Keeper. She wouldn't hold still.
src: 'I did my best, Keeper. She wouldn\'t hold still.'

k: She never would.
src: 'She never would.'

k: How long?
src: 'How long?'

k: A year. I meant to hold it for a minute. Just until the boat was clear.
src: 'A year. I meant to hold it for a minute. Just until the boat was clear.'

k: Something took hold of me afterwards. It kept saying, _not yet. Not yet. Keep her safe._ I think it was me. I'm sorry. I think it was only ever me.
src: 'Something took hold of me afterwards. It kept saying, _not yet. Not yet. Keep her safe._ I think it was me. I\'m sorry. I think it was only ever me.'

k: I'm sorry. I'm sorry I took the Dawnstone. I'm sorry about what I said at supper. I'm sorry I left. I'm sorry I didn't come home sooner—
src: 'I\'m sorry. I\'m sorry I took the Dawnstone. I\'m sorry about what I said at supper. I\'m sorry I left. I\'m sorry I didn\'t come home sooner—'

k: Wren. Little bird. Breathe.
src: 'Wren. Little bird. Breathe.'

k: I knew you would leave from the day you could walk. I wasn't angry that you wanted to go. I was angry that I was so afraid of it. Those aren't the same thing. It took me sixteen years and the end of the world to see it.
src: 'I knew you would leave from the day you could walk. I wasn\'t angry that you wanted to go. I was angry that I was so afraid of it. Those aren\'t the same thing. It took me sixteen years and the end of the world to see it.'

k: You went out after Dad. That night. I found your hand-lamp, tied to the Gull's Return.
src: 'You went out after Dad. That night. I found your hand-lamp, tied to the Gull\'s Return.'

k: ...You found it.
src: '...You found it.'

k: I left the Lantern dark for two hours. The only two hours in two hundred years. I looked for him until the oil ran out. Then I rowed home, because you were asleep in the house, and someone had to keep the light on for you.
src: 'I left the Lantern dark for two hours. The only two hours in two hundred years. I looked for him until the oil ran out. Then I rowed home, because you were asleep in the house, and someone had to keep the light on for you.'

k: You never told me. I thought for seven years you didn't even try.
src: 'You never told me. I thought for seven years you didn\'t even try.'

k: I know. I let you think it. It was easier to be the villain than to be the one who wasn't enough.
src: 'I know. I let you think it. It was easier to be the villain than to be the one who wasn\'t enough.'

k: I always thought you could have saved Dad. I thought it for seven years.
src: 'I always thought you could have saved Dad. I thought it for seven years.'

k: I know you did. I tried, Wren. Some day you might find out how hard. Don't hate me for not telling you.
src: 'I know you did. I tried, Wren. Some day you might find out how hard. Don\'t hate me for not telling you.'

k: I never hated you. I was just— sixteen.
src: 'I never hated you. I was just— sixteen.'

k: I remember sixteen. It's dreadful. I wouldn't do it twice for all the light in the world.
src: 'I remember sixteen. It\'s dreadful. I wouldn\'t do it twice for all the light in the world.'

k: Ilse. You kept her alive. I can see you did.
src: 'Ilse. You kept her alive. I can see you did.'

k: ...Someone had to carry the bandages.
src: '...Someone had to carry the bandages.'

k: Squire Kestrel. Late again.
src: 'Squire Kestrel. Late again.'

k: Sorry, Keeper.
src: 'Sorry, Keeper.'

k: Don't be. You came.
src: 'Don\'t be. You came.'

k: And you have a name now, I think. A real one.
src: 'And you have a name now, I think. A real one.'

k: Sable. Wren gave it to me. I kept it.
src: 'Sable. Wren gave it to me. I kept it.'

k: Good. Keep it. Keep it the way you'd keep a promise.
src: 'Good. Keep it. Keep it the way you\'d keep a promise.'

k: I'm Pip. I'm— a friend. Of hers. I steal things.
src: 'I\'m Pip. I\'m— a friend. Of hers. I steal things.'

k: Then you're welcome in my house, Pip. Don't steal the spoons. They were my mother's.
src: 'Then you\'re welcome in my house, Pip. Don\'t steal the spoons. They were my mother\'s.'

k: Ma'am.
src: 'Ma\'am.'

k: Bring them home.
src: 'Bring them home.'

k: They're not mine to bring.
src: 'They\'re not mine to bring.'

k: They are now.
src: 'They are now.'

k: Now. The light.
src: 'Now. The light.'

k: She holds out the lamp. Inside the brass, where the Dawnstone used to sleep, a piece of the broken sun.
src: 'She holds out the lamp. Inside the brass, where the Dawnstone used to sleep, a piece of the broken sun.'

k: A Keeper's light can't go out while the Keeper holds it. So I'm going to stop holding it. And you're going to carry it instead.
src: 'A Keeper\'s light can\'t go out while the Keeper holds it. So I\'m going to stop holding it. And you\'re going to carry it instead.'

k: I don't know how to be a Keeper. I never learned the Lantern. I left before you could teach me.
src: 'I don\'t know how to be a Keeper. I never learned the Lantern. I left before you could teach me.'

k: Oh, Wren. A Keeper isn't a lighthouse. A Keeper is someone who keeps a light going for the people still out in the dark. You've been doing it all year. I watched.
src: 'Oh, Wren. A Keeper isn\'t a lighthouse. A Keeper is someone who keeps a light going for the people still out in the dark. You\'ve been doing it all year. I watched.'

k: Not here. Not this island. Wherever you go.
src: 'Not here. Not this island. Wherever you go.'

k: Wren carries the Lanternkeeper's light. The *Lanternkeeper* Crest can now be equipped.
src: 'Wren carries the Lanternkeeper\'s light. The *Lanternkeeper* Crest can now be equipped.'

k: There. Oh, that's better. My hands were so tired.
src: 'There. Oh, that\'s better. My hands were so tired.'

k: Mom. Don't—
src: 'Mom. Don\'t—'

k: I have to, little bird. That's the whole point. That's what I was too afraid to learn.
src: 'I have to, little bird. That\'s the whole point. That\'s what I was too afraid to learn.'

k: I'm trying.
src: 'I\'m trying.'

k: I know. I can tell.
src: 'I know. I can tell.'

k: And for the first time in a year, the Lantern of Lanternfall goes out.
src: 'And for the first time in a year, the Lantern of Lanternfall goes out.'

k: For a moment there is nothing at all.
src: 'For a moment there is nothing at all.'

k: Then, in Wren's open hand, a small warm light. It does not need a Lantern.
src: 'Then, in Wren\'s open hand, a small warm light. It does not need a Lantern.'

k: ...She was nice. Your mum.
src: '...She was nice. Your mum.'

k: She was terrible. She was the best.
src: 'She was terrible. She was the best.'

k: Both. She was both.
src: 'Both. She was both.'

k: Yeah. Both is allowed.
src: 'Yeah. Both is allowed.'

k: I said goodbye to Mom. A real one, this time. She said a Keeper is someone who keeps a light going for people out in the dark. Then she let go, and the Lantern went out, and the light was in my hand. Grow up well, she said. I'm trying.
src: 'I said goodbye to Mom. A real one, this time. She said a Keeper is someone who keeps a light going for people out in the dark. Then she let go, and the Lantern went out, and the light was in my hand. Grow up well, she said. I\'m trying.'

k: The Lantern log of Lanternfall, open on its stand, two hundred years of weather and oil in neat columns. One page is creased, as if it has been opened to many times.
src: 'The Lantern log of Lanternfall, open on its stand, two hundred years of weather and oil in neat columns. One page is creased, as if it has been opened to many times.'
